questions.question: To what is Egypt (Pharaoh) compared in Ezekiel 31?
options: A boiling pot tipped from the north
A great vine bending toward a great second eagle
A great dragon lying in the rivers
A towering cedar of Lebanon, later cut down
questions.answer: A towering cedar of Lebanon, later cut down

questions.question: What lesson does the felled cedar teach?
options: That the strong will always rule over the weak in every age
That great wealth brings lasting security and safety to a nation
That pride leads to a fall; even mighty Assyria was brought down
That the great cedar would only grow taller than it was before
questions.answer: That pride leads to a fall; even mighty Assyria was brought down

questions.question: Ezekiel 31 uses Assyria as a cedar that was cut down, as a warning to Egypt.
Consider Assyria, a cedar in Lebanon; the waters nourished it, and it towered _____.
Because it towered high, its heart was _____ in its height.
